subject: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)
parts:
Suppose I have a function like this in an R package:

launch_my_app(X) {
  Y <- preprocess(X)   # where preprocess does a bunch of computations that I'd like to avoid doing inside of the Shiny app
  shiny::runApp(...)   # where ...  are the appropriate arguments to runApp 
}

where I'd the app to then use the object Y (e.g. do stuff to Y in server.R, etc.).

Of course, with Shiny's scoping rules this won't work, as Y will not be accessible. The only solution I've found is to assign Y to the user's global environment (e.g. using something like assign("Y", preprocess(X), inherits = TRUE)), in which case it works great. But this is part of an R package and so I'd like to avoid assignments to the global environment like this. 

Am I missing an easy way to make this work or, if not, does anyone have any clever ideas? 

Thanks in advance for the help,

Jonah

P.S. A similar question has been asked before, but there was no real solution offered (and the suggestions there won't work in my case).

messages.author: 8d697d8f528e19a5
messages.subject: Re: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)
parts:
Add the shiny::runApp() call to your server.R (I would place it at the end of the file). Then, your function becomes

launch_my_app(X) {
 Y <- preprocess(X)
 source(PATH_TO_SERVER.R)
}

Would this work?

Ben

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Calling runApp from within a function (scoping problems)
parts:
Since you're using a package, another option is to have an environment in your package for holding global-like variables that are scoped to your package. For example:

values <- new.env(parent=emptyenv())

Then when you launch shiny:

values$foo <- X
on.exit(values$foo <- NULL, add=TRUE)
shiny::runApp(...)

And in your app reference mypackage:::values$foo.
